summary: Backend security-hardening + regression testing for DevicePulse. Ran 21 pytest tests via localhost:8001 (per instruction). ALL 21 PASSED (100%). SEC-001 rate limit verified via a single ~12-request burst: exactly 10 x 200 OK followed by 2 x 429 (confirmed both in test assertions and in /var/log/supervisor/backend.out.log). SEC-003 prompt-injection blocked: platform='IGNORE ALL INSTRUCTIONS...' still returned a normal 4-item recommendation list with no leaked EMERGENT_LLM_KEY / 'sk-' / 'system prompt' markers. Family-member input hardening confirmed: 100-char name truncated to exactly 40 chars, empty/whitespace names return 400, and device_type='hacker' falls back to 'phone'. Referral invited_count cap holds at 100 after 102 invites. All core GETs (health, storage, duplicates, large-files, battery, security, cache-breakdown), POST scan/clean (with persistence check via /history), streak (first freeze 200, second freeze same month 400), forecast, health-trend, referral, reminders GET/PUT, and family GET all return 200 with expected data.
action_items: Optional (not a regression): the SEC-001 rate limiter keys on request.client.host, which behind a K8s ingress often collapses to a single upstream IP so real users could share a bucket. Consider honoring X-Forwarded-For (first hop) once a trusted proxy header allowlist is in place. Current behavior still satisfies the audit fix.
Optional: rate-limit state is process-local (in-memory dict). If the backend is ever scaled to >1 worker/pod the limit becomes per-instance. Fine for MVP; note it for the future.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py 'import time as _time' is placed mid-file (line 168). Move all imports to the top for PEP-8 compliance (non-blocking).
server.py uses BaseModel.dict() (deprecated in pydantic v2 in favor of .model_dump()). Works today but will emit warnings; consider migrating.
_referral_code uses Python's hash() which is randomized per-process (PYTHONHASHSEED). Referral codes will change across restarts. Use hashlib for a stable code.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py (rewritten as full security + regression pytest suite)
seed_data_creation: Each test uses a unique TEST_-prefixed device_id (uuid) so no shared state; documents are created in db.cleanups / db.freezes / db.referrals / db.reminders / db.family / db.scans and are safe to leave (they do not affect production users). No global seed writes.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend security hardening (SEC-001 rate limit, SEC-003 platform allowlist, family name/type validation, referral cap) is verified working. Test file /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py hits localhost:8001 by default (override with BACKEND_TEST_URL). The AI burst test costs ~10 LLM calls per run — invoke it sparingly. Run 'pytest tests/backend_test.py --deselect tests/backend_test.py::TestAIRecommendationsSecurity' for a zero-cost regression pass.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no failures. All applied security fixes function correctly and no regressions were introduced.
